proposal.text: The Tallahassee bus boycott helped end legally segregated seating on the city’s buses. On January 7, 1957, the city repealed its explicit segregation ordinance and gave drivers the power to assign seats. Riders who challenged that rule still faced arrest. Enforcement of assigned seating eased over the following months as Black riders returned. Florida Memory dates integration on Tallahassee’s buses to summer 1957.
